data.name: Mikail
data.gender_notes: Mikail is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'Makhluq' which means 'created'. It implies being like Allah or having the qualities of Allah. The name Mikail carries the meaning “Like Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mikail usually hope their child will grow to embody like allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The one who is like Allah, the Almighty.
data.etymology: Mikail belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Like Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mikail total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: ميكائيل
in_arabic.long_meaning: ميكائيل هو اسم ملاك كبير في الإسلام، وهو واحد من أربعة ملائكة كبار، ويتولى أمور الرزق والغيث، وله ذكر في القرآن الكريم، وفي الحديث النبوي الشريف، وهو اسم شائع في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: میکائیل
in_urdu.long_meaning: میکائیل ایک بڑے فرشتے کا نام ہے جو اسلام میں اہم ہے، وہ رزق اور بارش کا انچارج ہے، قرآن پاک میں اور حدیث نبوی میں اس کا ذکر ہے، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم ثقافت میں بہت مشہور ہے

in_hindi.name: मीकाएल
in_hindi.long_meaning: मीकाएल एक बड़े दूत का नाम है जो इस्लाम में महत्वपूर्ण है, वह रिज़क और वर्षा का प्रभारी है, कुरान और हदीस में इसका उल्लेख है, यह नाम भारतीय मुसलमान समुदाय में बहुत प्रसिद्ध है

data.cultural_impact: The name Mikail is of Arabic origin and is considered to be a variant of the Biblical name Michael. In Islamic tradition, Mikail is recognized as an angel who was entrusted with the responsibility of passing divine messages from Allah to Prophet Moses. This name is popular in the Islamic world and is often given to children as a sign of faith and admiration for this significant figure in Islamic history.
data.spiritual_significance: Mikail, being derived from the Arabic word 'Makhluq', signifies the notion of creation. As Muslims, we believe that all things in this universe are created by Allah. By giving a child the name Mikail, parents are not only acknowledging the fact that their child is a created being, but they are also implying that their child has the potential to embody the qualities of the Creator. The name is a reminder that every individual is a gift from Allah and has the capacity to be a reflection of His perfection.
